chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:

We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said to al-Hakam the tailor: 'What do you think regarding what is carried to Syria from the armor and its equipment?' He said: 'There is no harm; you today are in the position of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for you are in a truce. But when the allegiance (bay'ah) comes, it will be forbidden for you to carry to them the weapons and the armor.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Companions of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: When does carrying weapons become forbidden according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the dynamic nature of political allegiance in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between a period of temporary truce (*hudna*) where carrying arms is permissible, and the establishment of formal allegiance (*bay'ah*) which renders it forbidden. It underscores the principle that the permissibility of carrying weapons to the ruling authority is contingent upon the specific political and religious status of the community at that time.
